content: 1. School staff should conduct thorough inspections of the school environment to ensure it is safe and conducive to learning (I-24). 2. There should be a system in place for the referral and support of child caregivers, ensuring they receive the necessary resources and assistance (I-77). 3. Efforts should be made to promote positive health and development among children, including fostering healthy behaviors and environments (I-07). 4. The appropriate use of electronic devices should be encouraged, with an emphasis on minimizing excessive screen time and promoting balanced usage (I-08). 5. Adequate sleep should be promoted as a critical component of physical and mental health, particularly for children and adolescents (I-10). 6. Parenting skills should be supported and enhanced through targeted programs and interventions (I-10). 7. Developmental disabilities should be identified early through appropriate screening and assessment processes (I-30). 8. Counseling services should be provided to address developmental concerns and support children’s growth and well-being (I-43). 9. Psychosocial interventions should be implemented to promote mental health and overall well-being (I-45). 10. Caregivers should receive support and guidance related to their child’s development, ensuring they are equipped to meet their child’s needs (I-45c). 11. Education should be provided to prevent unintentional injuries, such as those occurring at home, during play, or on the road (I-48). 12. Systems should be in place for the referral and support of children who experience injuries, burns, or drowning incidents (I-70, I-71, I-72). 13. Violence prevention education should be provided universally, with a focus on reducing abuse and harmful practices (I-49, I-50). 14. Counseling services should be available to prevent violence and support victims of violence, including gender-based violence and child abuse (I-73). 15. Interventions should be categorized as essential or suitable within school health services (SHS), depending on the geographic location and specific needs of the population. 16. Health promotion activities should include timely care-seeking behaviors, health literacy, personal hygiene, oral health care, reduced sugar consumption, and increased physical activity (I-01 to I-06). 17. Adequate sun exposure should be promoted to prevent sunburn and overheating while ensuring sufficient vitamin D synthesis (I-11). 18. Menstrual hygiene management should be promoted, and sexual and reproductive health education should be provided to adolescents (I-09, I-15). 19. Screening programs should assess physical growth, motor development, social and emotional maturity, and other health concerns at key educational stages (I-28). 20. Immunizations should be provided universally, with additional focus on high-risk populations and specific regions (I-38 to I-41). 21. Counseling and referral services should address mental health concerns, substance use, and self-harm, with a focus on early intervention and crisis management (I-37, I-76, I-82). 22. Nutritional education and physical activity programs should be implemented to promote healthy lifestyles and prevent obesity (I-13, I-14). 23. Screening for vision, hearing, oral health, and nutrition problems should be conducted regularly to identify and address issues early (I-31 to I-35). 24. Support should be provided for children with chronic conditions, disabilities, or developmental delays, ensuring they receive appropriate care and resources (I-68, I-69). 25. Policies should be in place to support mental health promotion, bullying prevention, and anaphylaxis management within schools (I-21, I-22). 26. Referral and support systems should address conditions such as asthma, anemia, diabetes, and other chronic or acute health issues (I-66 to I-68). 27. Comprehensive sexuality education should include counseling on contraception, prevention of sexually transmitted infections, and HIV testing and prophylaxis (I-51 to I-55). 28. Management of infectious disease outbreaks should be prioritized, with mass drug administration and immunizations as preventive measures (I-38, I-61). 29. Support should be provided for adolescents experiencing pregnancy, ensuring they have the option to continue or return to school (I-74). 30. Counseling and referral services should address emotional, anxiety, and depressive disorders, as well as eating disorders and stress management (I-79 to I-81). 31. Systems should be in place to manage self-harm and suicide risk, providing immediate and long-term support (I-82). 32. Policies should support the prevention of harmful substance use and provide assistance for withdrawal and dependency management (I-86, I-87). 33. All interventions should be supported by WHO guidelines and evidence, ensuring they are implemented effectively and appropriately within school health services.
